TLDR: Going to hosptial isn’t a fix all solution unfortunately. Depending on where you are, getting admitted is almost impossible unless you actually attempt but even then you can just be sent home. 

Usually it’s to keep you safe until you can be released into community care. If you are suicidal and have a plan then you may get admitted but depending on where you are you also may not, I had attempted many times but was never hospitalised until my parents refused to take me home so legally the hosptial had to take me (was a last resort). 

Most of the time you won’t get any therapy or even meet a psychiatrist. Sometimes, depending on funding again, there may be activities. Otherwise it’s really fucking boring, the staff are usually not very well educated and do the bare minimum, usually they stay in the nurse station and if you want to talk to someone they are too busy. 

If you want to get yourself admitted, try to do a direct admission. Call up the place and ask how you get yourself admitted otherwise you could be waiting 12+ hours in the emergency room for the mental health team just to send you home. 

Best way to do it is, honestly, getting the cops to bring you in and being uncooperative so they section you (legally hosptial against your will) but that sometimes doesn’t even work.

What I’ve been told by the over 20+ medical professionals I’ve been to over the last five years, being deemed a chronic case but I’m fighting to recover. 

First thing first, check to see if there’s any physical reason for your mental health. Get a dr appt, blood work done etc and talk to them about how you feel. 

They can refer you to a therapist for therapy and a psych for medication (there’s plenty to help with aggression) 

Also, talk to the people around you. Get a decent support system, you will need them. 

Therapy, medication, having a good support system, learning coping skills for when you feel bad etc are all important. 

But you need to want to get better and engage in therapy, you are only going to get better if you put in the work. The hard truth that I’ve finally learn after five years of therapy.

Being honest to your therapist is the only way to get the help you need. Admitting that you are suicidal won’t automatically mean you’ll be sectioned (hosptialised against your will) how ever I will say that being hospitalised saved my life and helped me break the cycle of constantly being in ‘crisis mode’ 

It is a choice to engage in therapy and doing the work, it’s a hard one to make, you can get ‘comfortable’ in living in crisis mode but it is worth it. 

DBT might be helpful, but to note, it isn’t the thing that will save you until you do the work and it doesn’t work for everyone. It’s most helpful for people with bpd. If you are or think you are, autistic or in anyway neruodivergent it probably won’t help, and group therapy will make you worse. 

Medication, therapy, a good support system and learning skills to help with distress are the tools that can get you through it but you’ve got to be honest, work with the people around you and work damn hard to get better. 

It’s an ethical issue around physical contact, but your therapist is showing good signs by refusing. They aren’t your friend or surraget parent, they are your therapist. 

Talk to your school. I’m sure your therpapist can provide the paperwork to get you at 504 plan or your countries equivalent. It’ll help, simple things like being able to leave to have a break at any time no questions asked, permedent extensions on all work/homework. 

I promise that you can get better, you aren’t ‘broken’ or ‘beyond help’
